name: sshi_fbr_zener
rationale: Implements a Parallel Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) circuit combined with a full-bridge rectifier and a Zener clamp. The inductor-switch combination flips the piezoelectric capacitance voltage at the extrema, significantly increasing energy extraction efficiency over a standard FBR. This should fix the vavg and tup failures in S2 and S4. The DZ33 Zener diode clamps the output voltage to avoid exceeding the 3.6V limit in S3 (strong excitation).

name: sshi_fbr_no_zener
rationale: Same as sshi_fbr_zener but without the Zener clamp. This explores whether the energy harvester can be stabilized within the 1.8V-3.6V range purely through the load and storage capacitor without clamping, potentially improving efficiency for the lower-power cases (S2, S4).

name: fbr_zener_large_c
rationale: A simplified approach applying only the Zener clamp and a larger storage capacitor to the baseline FBR. This tests if the instability (dv) and overvoltage (vmax) seen in the reference design can be resolved simply by clamping and increasing inertia, without the complexity of active switching.

problems: design 1 (doubler_zener): Dz: nodes ["out", "0"] put the anode on out, so the diode is forward-biased, holds out near 0.3-0.7 V and drains the storage. A zener clamp on out needs nodes ["0", "out"] (cathode on out)

name: doubler_zener
rationale: The previous SSHI design suffered from excessive ripple and slow settling due to the large output capacitor needed to buffer its high-energy bursts. The reference FBR design was smooth and fast-settling but lacked the voltage to meet vout_min on S2 and S4. A voltage doubler (Greinacher) is proposed here. It provides a voltage boost (roughly 2x the piezo voltage) to ensure vout_min is met, while avoiding the spiky current pulses of the SSHI. By using a smaller output capacitor (Cout), we can simultaneously satisfy the 'settled' (fast time constant for RL=1M Ohm) and 'startup' requirements, while the inherent smoothness of the doubler maintains low ripple. Corrected the Zener orientation to prevent forward-biasing the output.

name: sshi_pi_filter
rationale: The previous best design (sshi_fbr_zener) failed only on S3 ripple (62mV vs 50mV). This ripple is caused by the periodic charge pulses from the SSHI rectifier into the storage capacitor. To reduce this ripple without increasing the output capacitor to a point where start-up (tup) or stability (dv) fail, I am adding a Pi-filter (C-L-C) between the rectifier and the load. The first capacitor (C1) buffers the rectifier pulses, and the subsequent LC filter (L2, C2) smooths the voltage delivered to the load, significantly reducing peak-to-peak ripple.
